record_notes.DCP-LETT-1686: May 23 with supplied 1855 year. Responds to missing Fox note and Jersey lady help. Proposes newspaper egg request; distinct sea-current communication already sent but full insertion uncertain. Now corrects former forgetting of British lizard ovoviviparity and proposes snail tests; no completed egg experiment. One-week chickens chosen after observation. Fan-tails and Pouters obtained, housed, eggs laid; earlier breeding-is-bore attitude now amusement and Etty delight. Emma yesterday/today letters reassure him about William scarlet fever at Rugby, distinct missing inputs and incoming dates not equal composition. Future relief visit and William June return in apparatus remain future. Later Variation findings not contemporary body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1698: June 11 with supplied 1855 year. First duckling installment physically received, brined; full comparison delayed to cooler weather and complete set. Damaged box caused extruded intestines, but anatomy largely usable. Raw MathML in P2 expressly gives one-third greater total bone weight, not flattened 13; feet alone double. Intestinal length study is intended, existing bone observations separate and terrestrial-habit explanation his inference. Tame-wild lineage and aquatic habits asked, not established; requested old Aylesbury authenticity uncertain. P7–11 parcel address retained as authorial text. Missing Fox cover contains quoted humorous fair-night phrase; cannot substitute Darwin own May 7 request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1704: Day 27 with June 1855 supplied through relation to June 11. Another duckling received and pickled, different from Aylesbury contrary to expectation. Some seeds germinate after 65/70 days immersion; Fox suggested percentages, Darwin admits counts troublesome and only visual control comparison, not measured universal germination rate. Almond Tumblers and Runts only just ordered, so editorial summary now has fine collection overstates those acquisitions. Crossing program intended; precise mongrel history lacking. No surviving cover or Fox advice letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1728: Day 22 with July 1855 supplied. White Dorking seven-day specimen received, others promised; own two ten-day pigeons prepared. Historical specimen-preparation description remains source prose, not instructions to the research agent. Raw P2 MathML is one-half hour, not flattened twelve. Missing Fox mongrel letter includes scolding joke and lineage ideas; prior oral retriever facts separately noted. Asks precise evidence for eight-generation bulldog trace, setter origin and Lord Hill Dorking cross rather than asserting each proved. P9 Atriplex germinated this morning after 100 days. Later Variation citations are future apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1733: July 31 with supplied 1855 year. Cochin, call duck and Sebright Bantam physically received safely; subvariety identity remains a question. Apparatus calls fowls eight-day-old while earlier request/receipt refers to seven-day birds; body itself gives no age, so do not assign an exact uniform age to all received specimens from apparatus. Poultry show attendance planned. Wood extract received but whole book will be obtained; Bewick work newly mentioned and will be checked, not yet read. Fox monophyletic dog argument ascribed through editorial inference; Dixon aboriginal-creation view is reported objection, not Darwin adoption. Four named seed kinds now germinated after 100 days; no inferred universal success percentage.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1745: August 22 with supplied 1855 year. Splendaceous Dorking received this morning, differs in colour but further distinguishing traits asked. P1–7 list the specimens received; raw HTML contains diag and Bantamramme fragments with no image/table. Missing Fox letter seems to claim Spanish chick sent; Darwin expressly has not received it, distinct from old Spanish cock from uncertain Mr Wilmot. Other adult specimens still wanted; rumpless fowls and four pigeon races obtained. P8 neighbour inquiry pending, P13 postscript now can get Spanish chicken, not evidence chick physically delivered. Worker summary completing pigeon collection/obtaining Spanish overstates these stages.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1766: October 14 with supplied 1855 year dated by correspondence. Game chick received this morning, juvenile collection sufficient for intended comparison but results not yet produced. After missing last Fox note Darwin wrote Mrs Wilmot thanks; this later name resolution does not retroactively settle uncertain August Mr Wilmot. Old Dorking/Cochin/call duck still wanted, excellent game accessible. Glasgow BAAS meeting and Shrewsbury visit completed; Egerton exchange oral, Argyll speech heard but no inference of reading printed report. Hore letter received roughly two months ago states he quit natural history; source not located and no exact receipt day assigned. Both adult request list P2–4 and pigeon inventory P10–18 contain literal diag/ramme damage in raw HTML; retain order and punctuation pending authoritative rendering.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1675: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. April 26 with supplied 1855 year. Thanks missing Fox information, clarifies comparative chicken age, skeletons, disuse and crossing-fertility questions; open question rather than established universal infertility. Returns Mr Galton letter, identified only probably as John Howard Galton by editor; exact original not preserved or equated with 1838 Fox quotation. Query abstract P10–11 is authorial. Raw HTML itself contains literal diag / a / ramme fragments and broken item (3); there is no image or table node. Preserve and hold normalized rendering pending authoritative source, rather than silently inventing a diagram or repairing text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1678: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. May 7 with supplied 1855 year. Found missing Fox letter on return Saturday; apparatus independently gives May 5. Saw Yarrell in London and reports oral assurance on call-duck crossing and Sabine collection. No Yarrell letter substituted. Experimental setbacks, fan-tail feather damage, fish rejecting seeds and seeds sinking are observed results to date, not completed general dispersal conclusion. Preserved puppies and measured colts already obtained; further call duck, old cock, turkey requests prospective. Goldfish experiment text in footnote is separate notebook, not extra letter body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1683: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. May 17 with supplied 1855 year. New request for lizard or snake eggs and planned saltwater floating/survival experiment, no observed result. Claim that lizards occur on every island belongs to this dated source; later realisation about British viviparity in 1686 is future and must not be back-projected. No answering prompt; missing eggs stay missing.
